facts.text: Blood Diner was shot in just three weeks on a budget of only about $330,000.
Director Jackie Kong says distributors were stunned to meet her after the film's success. They had assumed she was a man, since women directing movies was almost unheard of then.
The film's 'cult of Sheetar' echoes Blood Feast, where the killer was Fuad Ramses and the goddess Ishtar. Here the killer becomes Anwar Namtut and the goddess Sheetar.
Little Michael, the wrestling-obsessed kid hero's pint-sized pal? Not quite: the character Little Michael was played by a woman, actress Roxanne Osco.
Screenwriter Michael Sonye wrote under the pseudonym 'Dukey Flyswatter' and also appears in the film. He acted in Troma's Surf Nazis Must Die the same year.
The score was composed by Don Preston, a former keyboardist with Frank Zappa's Mothers of Invention. Filmmaker Robert Downey Sr. reportedly introduced him to Jackie Kong.

Anwar's boast that Sheetar is 'more powerful than Superman' is one of the film's pop-culture nods. The IMDb connections list also credits Superman (1978), Flashdance and King Kong Lives as references.
Vitamin's crack about cheerleaders dressed up like 'Flashdance' is one of the movie's 1980s pop shout-outs. Flashdance came out in 1983, four years earlier.
Kong said she avoided watching Blood Feast so it wouldn't influence her film. One Blu-ray reviewer at Genre Grinder doubts that claim.
Carl Crew, who plays George Tutman, joked in the Blu-ray extras that Tanya Papanicolas, who plays the goddess Sheetar, 'always smelled like teriyaki.'
Wrestling fans may spot the TV in Georgie's room: a figurine in front of it keeps vanishing and reappearing between shots.
Per an archival interview with project consultant Eric Caidin, the brothers were originally meant to be played by horror face Michael Berryman and pro wrestler George 'The Animal' Steele.
Blood Diner's UK 18-certificate release was cut by 3 minutes 53 seconds by the BBFC, and the UK Vestron tape was heavily trimmed.
Punk and rockabilly musicians were cast as extras, bit players and even leads. Writer Michael Sonye himself played in the punk band Haunted Garage, making the club scenes a love letter to 1987 LA.
Blood Diner was banned in a number of Canadian provinces on release.
The 1988 Australian Vestron home video, rated R, is the uncut version. The German rental tape and UK sale tape were cut, while the Dutch tape was uncut.

Director Jackie Kong says the script was 'as serious as a heart attack' until she added the comedy. Writer Michael Sonye disputes that, saying producer Jimmy Maslon's ideas had to be funny to be used.
Blood Diner was Jackie Kong's third feature, after The Being (1983) and Night Patrol (1984). A Blu-ray extra says the cast was assembled without SAG support.
The nature hike was filmed at Bronson Caves in Griffith Park, Los Angeles. It's a classic movie location, and that's also where the film's Hollywood shooting took place.
Writer Michael Sonye cites The Evil Dead and Re-Animator as major influences on Blood Diner's gory-funny tone, even though director Jackie Kong insists nobody was making horror-comedies before 1987.
The film's soundtrack leans on 1950s doo-wop: The Penguins, The Calvanes, The Meadowlarks and The Medallions all appear, mixed with new rockabilly from Dino Lee.
Much of the dialogue was post-synced, and reviewers note the sync is often rough, which fits the rough-edged sound of Herschell Gordon Lewis's Blood Feast.
Directed by Jackie Kong, Blood Diner was produced by Lawrence Kasanoff, Kong, Jimmy Maslon and Ellen Steloff. Maslon also wrote the song 'Shake It Out'.
Director Jackie Kong wanted Blood Diner released unrated instead of trimmed for an R from the MPAA. Distributor Vestron agreed.
The film got only a limited theatrical release from Lightning Pictures in July 1987, then found its audience on VHS from Vestron Video.
Rick Burks, who plays Michael Tutman, died in 1989 at age 29, so he is absent from the 2016 making-of documentary.
Lionsgate launched its Vestron Video Collector's Series in 2016 with Blood Diner. Director Jackie Kong agreed to record a commentary only if the studio also backed a theatrical run.
The rockabilly tune 'Stud Pony' was written and performed by Dino Lee, who also provided 'Everybody Get Some' for the film.
Vestron's closure meant director Jackie Kong finished only two pictures of her three-picture deal with the company.
The official Blood Feast sequel finally came in 2002: Herschell Gordon Lewis made Blood Feast 2: All U Can Eat, 15 years after Blood Diner.
Blood Diner sold out Fantastic Fest, and Fangoria reports midnight crowds respond with a Rocky Horror-style frenzy. Fans have even had the film tattooed on their bodies.
TV Guide felt the film paid tribute to Herschell Gordon Lewis but that Jackie Kong's contempt for the source material left little of value. Rotten Tomatoes sits at 50%.
Carl Crew, who plays George Tutman, mentioned in the Blu-ray extras a possible sequel called Blood Dinner, which he said would be shot entirely in virtual reality.
In 2016 Jackie Kong took Blood Diner on a roadshow with Q&As and rock 'n roll parties in Austin, Denver, Kansas City and New York to promote the Vestron Blu-ray.
